records.title: Pretrained Model with CNN for Lung Cancer Identification and Classification
records.abstract: Lung cancer impacts both genders, and its early detection is key to lowering death rates. Current deep learning techniques for automated identification and classification of lung carcinoma face issues with interpretability, data variability handling, and broader applicability. In our research, we propose a novel method that merges a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a streamlined RESNET18 framework. This approach is designed for lung cancer detection and categorization from CT scans, involving image preprocessing like resizing and rescaling. It effectively differentiates between healthy and cancerous tissues, further classifying them as either Normal, Benign, or Malignant, including variants such as adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. Our CNN+RESNET18 model boasts an impressive 99% accuracy, supporting radiologists in the intricate task of image analysis, reducing risks of incorrect or delayed diagnosis, and fostering prompt treatment for improved patient outcomes.

records.title: Application of Several Transfer Learning Approach for Early Classification of Lung Cancer
records.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lung cancer, a fatal disease characterized by abnormal cell growth, ranks as the second most lethal worldwide, as observed in recent research conducted in India and other regions. Early detection is crucial for effective treatment, and manual differentiation of nodule types in CT images poses challenges for radiologists. OBJECTIVES: To enhance accuracy and efficiency, deep learning algorithms are proposed for early lung cancer detection. Transfer learning-based computer recognition algorithms have shown promise in providing radiologists with additional insights. METHODS: The dataset used in this study comprises 1000 CT scan images representing lung large cell carcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma, lung squamous cell carcinoma, and normal lung cases. A preprocessing phase, including picture rescaling and modification, is applied to the input CT scan images of the lungs, followed by the utilization of a specific transfer learning model to develop a lung cancer detection system. RESULTS: The performance of various transfer learning strategies is evaluated using measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, area under the curve, and F1-score. CONCLUSION: Comparative analysis indicates that VGG16 outperforms other models in accurately categorizing different types of lung cancer.

records.title: Regulation of Oncogenic Targets by Tumor-Suppressive miR-150-3p in Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma
records.abstract: Several recent studies have shown that both strands of certain miRNAs derived from miRNA duplexes are involved in cancer pathogenesis. Our own recent studies revealed that both strands of the miR-150 duplex act as tumor-suppressive miRNAs in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) through the targeting of several oncogenes. The aim of the study here was to further investigate the tumor-suppressive roles of miR-150-3p (the passenger strand) in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSQ) and its control of cancer-promoting genes in LUSQ cells. The downregulation of miR-150-3p in LUSQ tissues was confirmed by data in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). The ectopic expression of miR-150-3p attenuated cancer cell aggressive features, e.g., cell cycle arrest, migration and invasive abilities. Our target search strategy successfully identified a total of 49 putative targets that were listed as subjects of miR-150-3p regulation in LUSQ cells. Interestingly, among these targets, 17 genes were categorized as related to the “cell cycle” based on Gene Ontology (GO) classification, namely CENPA, CIT, CCNE1, CCNE2, TIMELESS, BUB1, MCM4, HELLS, SKA3, CDCA2, FANCD2, NUF2, E2F2, SUV39H2, CASC5, ZWILCH and CKAP2). Moreover, we show that the expression of HELLS (helicase, lymphoid specific) is directly controlled by miR-150-3p, and its expression promotes the malignant phenotype of LUSQ cells.

records.title: Multi-Class Lung Cancer Classification Using a Multi-Axis Attention-Based Deep Learning Framework
records.abstract: Lung cancer is one of the most common causes of death from cancer worldwide and timely, accurate diagnosis helps improve patient survival rates. Deep learning techniques have already proven their amazing capabilities of automating disease detection from medical images and such techniques can be immensely helpful to all healthcare practitioners. The proposed deep learning-based framework for automatic classification of lung cancer types using chest CT scan images. The proposed method leverages a transformer architecture called MaxViT, which, unlike conventional transformers that rely on regular granularity, increases the granularity of each image region via fine-grained convolutional neural networks and incorporates multi-axis attention modules to capture both low-level or high-order features. The research study uses a collection of chest CT scan images which are divided into four categories: Adenocarcinoma, Large cell carcinoma, Squamous cell carcinoma and Normal lung. The image preprocessing procedure begins with resizing and RGB space conversion before it transforms the image into tensor format which makes it suitable for deep learning model training. The proposed system uses Stratified K-Fold Cross Validation as its training method which helps to strengthen model performance while reducing overfitting risks by ensuring that each class appears in every training fold. The MaxViT based model was tested on 10-fold Stratified Cross-Validation. The model reached a validation accuracy of 94.64% because it showed identical performance across all testing sections. This study has significant findings about possible uses of a new deep learning-based diagnostic system for lung cancer-specific purposes by using computer assistance in providing physicians with more reliable and earlier means of diagnosing lung cancer.

records.title: Hybrid 3D–2D CNN for Four-Class Lung Lesion Classification
records.abstract: The paper proposes a lightweight and interpretable 3D-2D hybrid convolutional neural network architecture for multi-institutional four-class classification of lung lesions, including Adenocarcinoma, Large Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, and Normal. This model has been proposed to efficiently classify lung lesions based on images acquired through a chest CT scan. This proposed model is efficient and has an effective 2D separable-conv encoder to achieve high-resolution features in an image, a shallow 3D fusion block to achieve short-range Z context, an attention gating module to achieve feature selection, and a lightweight classifier to efficiently classify images while meeting deployment constraints. This research has proposed a lightweight and interpretable deep learning model to classify lung lesions based on images acquired through a chest CT scan. This deep learning model is efficient and can classify lung lesions into four classes, including Adenocarcinoma, Large Cell Carcinoma, Squamous Cell Carcinoma, and Normal. The proposed method has achieved an overall accuracy of 93.06%, precision of 95.53%, and F1-score of 93.84% on the held-out test set with a low parameter count for fast training and deployment.
